title: Regions, zones and the private backbone, and what leaving one costs

videos.script: You are about to work on Google Cloud for twenty-six lessons. You will not need a Google account for any of them. {{lab}} Three programs on your own computer stand in for it. The real Google Cloud command line. The Pub/Sub emulator, which Google ships with it. And Terraform, which says exactly what it would ask Google to build. {{tools}} What none of them can do is pretend to be the rest of Google Cloud. So some lessons run, some plan, and some are read. Each one tells you which. {{registers}} This lesson builds the lab, step by step, and shows what to do when a step fails. Then it asks the real Google a question, and reads the refusal. {{refusal}} Where is Google Cloud? It is a set of regions, each a place on the map. Inside each region sit zones. A zone is a separate failure, with its own power and its own network. {{zones}} Between the regions runs Google's own fibre. By default, your users join it near where they are. {{backbone}} And every arrow between two boxes has a price. Between two zones, a cent per gibibyte. Leaving São Paulo, fourteen cents, wherever the data goes. {{prices}} By the end, you can say where things are, and what it costs to move between them. {{end}}
